name: go-jwt-middleware-f4019a8c-blind27-ots
instr:
# go-jwt-middleware gives wrong answers on token intake, setup checks and key caching, without a test suite

The repository has received 27 separate undocumented edits. What this library guards is an HTTP service, and an equivalent for remote procedure calls, that admits a caller only when the caller presents a signed token, and optionally also proves it holds the key that token is tied to. Nothing about the wire format changed and no calling code changed, yet callers that used to be admitted are now turned away, callers that used to be turned away are now let through, and settings that used to be accepted at start-up are now refused.

Handing the guard a request that carries credentials goes wrong in several independent ways. A request bearing two authorization headers — two plain ones, two proof-bound ones, or one of each — is now admitted, where it used to be refused with the complaint that more than one is not allowed; a request with a single header still yields its token and the scheme it was sent under. Asking for the token from a named cookie fails immediately with a complaint that the name is empty, whatever name you pass, and passing a genuinely empty name no longer produces that complaint. Asking for it from a named query parameter yields nothing even when the parameter is present and carries a value, though the empty-name failure and the present-but-empty-value case still behave.
